analyst_view.overall: Early view: AEK pushed Real Madrid hard before losing 3-2 to a 93rd-minute Valverde goal, but they are 29th on three points and need wins. Galatasaray are 18th on six points after beating Stuttgart 2-0 with two early Batrakov goals, and they were top of the Super Lig at the last check. Aboubakary Koita's red card (shown after full time for protesting) means at least a ban for matchday 5; whether UEFA adds more games should be checked before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Galatasaray conceded nine in their first three league-phase games before the clean sheet against Stuttgart, and AEK have let in 11 in four, while both sides scored freely in their last outings (AEK twice against Real Madrid, Galatasaray 4-0 at Konyaspor in the league).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, AEK slightly ahead. I see nothing that moves it: both teams attack through the middle as much as the flanks, and with the win probabilities nearly level, neither should spend the game camped in its own box.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: a Greek-Turkish game in Athens comes with an edge, AEK need points badly, and Koita's dismissal for protesting at Real Madrid shows how heated their nights can get.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean slightly higher: both defences have been open in this competition and both teams have forwards who shoot early (Osimhen and Leão for Galatasaray, Jović and Varga for AEK in their last predicted line-up).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean higher, in line with the goals: Galatasaray put two on target and in within 15 minutes against Stuttgart, and AEK got enough efforts on goal to score twice against Real Madrid.
